# Introduction

This workflow starts either from an existing Bioconductor GRanges object or
from annotation/signal files, inspects the resulting records, and returns
ranges to Bioconductor methods. Refer to [Getting started](getting-started.html)
for the synthetic data model and coordinate conventions. Package website:
<https://renscq.github.io/GeneTrackR/>.

# Enter from existing GRanges {#existing-granges}

These intervals are constructed in an external range workflow; no GeneTrackR
file reader is involved. Coordinates already use the internal 1-based closed
convention. Range names, unused sequence levels, object metadata and supported
column annotations are retained through ordinary feature-level conversions.

```{r granges-input}
library(GeneTrackR)

external <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(
  "chr1",
  IRanges::IRanges(
    start = c(12341000L, 12339900L),
    end = c(12341100L, 12340000L)
  ),
  seqlengths = c(chr1 = 20000000L, chr2 = 30000000L)
)
names(external) <- c("late_region", "early_region")
external$category <- factor(
  c("late", "early"),
  levels = c("early", "late", "unused")
)
external$score <- S4Vectors::Rle(c("4.5", "2.5"))
S4Vectors::metadata(external) <- list(source = "external_range_workflow")
features <- as_feature(external)
features$data$category <- factor(
  c("reviewed", "late"),
  levels = c("early", "late", "unused", "reviewed")
)
returned <- as_granges(features, level = "feature")
returned
```

Feature's usual genomic sorting changes row order. Standard identifiers become
character, scores numeric, and exon numbers integer. Extra factor levels are
retained; Rle retains its container with normalized current values. Typed List
edits must be representable without loss. Fractional IntegerList edits fail
explicitly. Empty List columns retain source-container metadata, including
shared factor levels. See `?as_feature` for complete rules and rejected layouts.

```{r range-query}
selected <- retrieve_feature(
  features,
  chrom = "chr1",
  start = 12339800L,
  end = 12340100L
)
as_granges(selected, level = "feature")
query <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1", IRanges::IRanges(12339950L, 12340050L))
hits <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(returned, query)
returned[S4Vectors::queryHits(hits)]

figure_style <- ggplot2::theme(
  text = ggplot2::element_text(
    family = "Arial",
    colour = "black",
    face = "plain"
  )
)
plot_feature_track(
  features,
  chrom = "chr1",
  start = 12339001L,
  end = 12352000L,
  plot_theme = "classic",
  text_size = 10
) + figure_style
```

Ordinary intervals do not imply exons or CDS. Gene models require explicit
annotation relationships. Gene-model rebuilding can replace records and lose
per-feature metadata; conversion then fails explicitly. Subset the original
GRanges before such rebuilding when those metadata must be retained.

# Annotation files and gene models {#gene-models}

Readers convert source-format coordinates at the boundary. BED uses 0-based
half-open coordinates; GTF/GFF3 and internal Feature intervals are 1-based
closed. Do not apply another shift after reading.

```{r annotation-input}
demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "GeneTrackR")
gp <- read_genepred(
  file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo.genePredExt"),
  format = "genePredExt",
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
gtf <- read_gtf(
  file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo.gtf"),
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
gff <- read_gff(
  file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo.gff3"),
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
bed <- read_bed(
  file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo_features.bed"),
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
head(as_feature_table(bed))
summary_feature(gp, level = "gene")
validate_feature(gp)$invalid_summary
```

GenePred-compatible objects contain explicit gene/transcript/exon tables.
`as_genepred()` requires that information; it does not infer a gene model from
unrelated peaks. Gene, transcript and exon GRanges exports are summary
projections, while `level = "feature"` retains the flat annotation records.

```{r gene-and-transcript}
plot_gene(gp, gene_id = "GeneA", plot_theme = "classic", text_size = 10) +
  figure_style
gene <- retrieve_feature(gp, gene_id = "GeneA")
as_granges(gene, level = "transcript")
```

`plot_transcript()` supports genomic/spliced coordinates; gene plotting also
supports transcript-collapse, strand-direction, label and highlight controls.
These settings are described in the function reference and advanced-parameter
help rather than repeated as separate tutorials.

## Length quality control by segment and transcript

Gene spans include introns; spliced transcript lengths sum exons. Segment-level
CDS/UTR lengths use explicit genomic intersections and strand-aware UTR sides.

```{r length-segments}
segments <- get_gene_length_distribution_table(
  gp,
  feature = "cds",
  unit = "segment"
)
head(segments)
cds_totals <- aggregate(length_bp ~ transcript_id, data = segments, FUN = sum)
head(cds_totals)
```

Transcript-level exon/CDS/UTR summaries return one row per transcript and
feature. Their lengths sum the feature's segments rather than the bounding
genomic span, which may contain introns. The direct CDS summary agrees with
the explicit aggregation above:

```{r length-transcript-totals}
transcript_cds <- get_gene_length_distribution_table(
  gp,
  feature = "cds",
  unit = "transcript"
)
head(transcript_cds)
```

CDS/UTR use these transcript totals with `unit = "auto"`; exons use individual
segments with `unit = "auto"`. Distinct transcripts with equal lengths remain
separate observations. Non-coding records without CDS segments are absent from
this CDS table. The 0.99.6 correction removes repeated summary rows without
changing segment extraction, coordinates or inclusive length calculations.

# Signal tracks {#signal-tracks}

`read_bwg()` provides one BwgTrack workflow for bedGraph, WIG and BigWig. Sample
names identify separate tracks, not biological replicates inferred by the
package. RNA-seq and Ribo-seq demo values are synthetic signals in arbitrary
units. Do not compare samples on a common scale without justified normalization.

```{r signal-input}
signal_files <- c(
  "gtr_demo_rnaseq_plus.bedgraph",
  "gtr_demo_riboseq_plus.bedgraph"
)
signal <- read_bwg(
  file.path(demo_dir, signal_files),
  sample_names = c("RNA_seq_plus", "Ribo_seq_plus"),
  strand = c("+", "+"),
  mode = "memory",
  verbose = FALSE
)
signal_gr <- retrieve_bwg(
  signal,
  chrom = "chr1",
  start = 12339001L,
  end = 12352000L,
  as = "GRanges"
)
head(signal_gr)

plot_tracks(
  annotation = gp,
  signal = signal,
  gene_id = "GeneA",
  strand = "+",
  samples = c("RNA_seq_plus", "Ribo_seq_plus"),
  signal_type = "bar",
  signal_colors = c(RNA_seq_plus = "#4477AA", Ribo_seq_plus = "#228833"),
  layout = "gene_top",
  plot_theme = "classic",
  text_size = 10
) & figure_style
```

In memory mode the signal table is loaded immediately. Lazy mode retains file
metadata for regional access. Indexed bedGraph queries can use a system tabix
or optional Rsamtools; otherwise the documented full-file fallback applies.
BigWig uses the existing native reader. Query small regions first for large
data, and retain sample/strand/normalization metadata with exported values.
`norm_bwg()`, `bin_bwg()` and `merge_bwg()` expose explicit transformations;
consult their parameter and normalization-state rules before applying them.

## Transcript coordinates and Ribo-seq reading frames {#reading-frame}

Spliced transcript coordinates remove intronic distance. The frame view maps
P-site-like signal positions to CDS frame0/frame1/frame2 for a selected
transcript; it is not defined for an arbitrary genomic region.

```{r riboseq-reading-frame}
frame_view <- plot_signal_transcript(
  signal = signal,
  annotation = gp,
  transcript_id = "TxA1",
  samples = "Ribo_seq_plus",
  coordinate = "transcript",
  plot_type = "frame",
  strand = "auto",
  frame_colors = c(frame0 = "#4477AA", frame1 = "#EE6677", frame2 = "#228833"),
  signal_track_height = 4,
  gene_track_height = 1,
  direction_mode = "end",
  plot_theme = "classic",
  text_size = 10
)
frame_view & figure_style
```

The synthetic Ribo-seq data have a dominant frame-0 signal and lower irregular
frame-1/frame-2 counts to exercise this display. The plot is not a statistical
periodicity test or evidence of translation in a real biological sample.

# Class and I/O decisions {#design-decisions}

The current S3 structures and readers are retained to preserve existing code,
saved objects, analysis conventions and workflow state during this review
cycle. Standard Bioconductor representations remain the interoperability
boundary. A wrapper's convenience alone does not establish that a separate
parser or class is necessary.

| Structure | Current role and interoperability | Limitation / next evaluation |
|---|---|---|
| Feature / GenePred | Flat intervals, derived primary-model tables and an optional exon/CDS GRangesList grouped by transcript | The TxDb mapping assessment checks exon and CDS membership. Hierarchy rebuilds that would discard parent metadata are rejected. |
| VariantTrack | Point variants, raw FORMAT/sample fields, lazy-file metadata and GRanges export | Optional `CollapsedVCF` adapters retain a typed source for conversion and genotype export via VariantAnnotation. Native `write_vcf()` output remains sites-only. |
| BwgTrack | Multi-sample file/mode, strand and normalization state; in-memory and retrieved regions can export GRanges | Existing native parsers remain; standard-reader equivalence and platform/resource comparisons are still needed. |
| HapVariant / HapRefined / LDTrack | Related tables, parameters, group assignments and matrices used by downstream plots | These are workflow results. Replacing them with standard containers would require explicit schema and migration tests. |

For I/O, `rtracklayer::import()` and the lightweight Bioc.gff package are
relevant annotation-reader candidates, and `VariantAnnotation::readVcf()` is
relevant to VCF. Rsamtools is already reused for indexed queries. The current
native layer preserves a pure-R core and its existing defaults; this is a
compatibility decision, not a claim of superiority over standard readers.

Evidence includes read/write regressions, indexed VCF queries and
metadata-preserving GRanges conversions. The 0.99.9 adapters use
VariantAnnotation at the typed VCF boundary. The developer assessment compares
TxDb hierarchy mappings and indexed VCF reads with a shared POS query. Native
backends remain the default. New classes require an interoperability justification under the
[Bioconductor reuse guidance](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/reusebioc.html).

The 0.99.7 developer assessment compares shared GFF3, GTF, BED6, BED12, BigWig
and VCF fixtures with `rtracklayer`, `Bioc.gff` and `VariantAnnotation`. On the
recorded Windows environment, all eight reader comparisons match every input
record without unmatched records. Equality is checked on the fields explicitly
listed in the reports, rather than inferred from matching row counts.

The 0.99.8 follow-up retains complete parent metadata and BED12 structure while
keeping the existing classes and primary-parent analysis model:

- GFF3 `parent_ids` is a character-list column retaining all raw Parent tokens,
  including percent escapes. `parent_id` remains the first parent and the
  derived model is unchanged. Regenerated attributes preserve the complete
  list; edits must keep the primary field consistent with its first entry.
  Default `keep_attributes = TRUE` continues to reuse the original text.
- BED12 remains flat Feature records, now retaining `block_count`, `block_sizes`,
  `block_starts`, `thick_start`, `thick_end` and `item_rgb`. Sizes are widths in
  bp; block starts are zero-based offsets from the interval start. Thick spans
  are 1-based closed; `thick_end == thick_start - 1` denotes an empty span.
  The metadata-aware writer preserves repeated record names and validates edits.
- VCF point coordinates, generated missing IDs and rectangular typed genotype
  arrays can differ from `VariantAnnotation` representations. Agreement on the
  tested INFO/FORMAT fields is not a full typed-header or lossless-VCF contract.

The real-data assessment in 0.99.11 compares an indexed 1000 Genomes chr22
subset with VariantAnnotation and the GENCODE v19 chr22 GFF3 with rtracklayer.
On Windows and Linux, all 8,770 VCF records with POS inside the query matched
across five samples. One additional deletion overlapped the left boundary.
All 58,721 GFF3 records matched, including 57,458 Parent relationships.
The reports record the fields compared, input hashes, package versions,
read times and peak memory in `tools/io-evaluation/0.99.11-assessment.md`
in the source checkout. macOS and larger VCF cohorts remain to be evaluated.

## Preserve shared parents and BED12 structure

The primary-model rebuild in `retrieve_feature()` now fails explicitly if
complete parent links would be discarded. Filter the flat
GRanges representation to keep every original record and its metadata:

```{r annotation-parent-metadata}
gff_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".gff3")
gff_lines <- c(
  "##gff-version 3",
  "chr1\tfixture\tgene\t1\t20\t.\t+\t.\tID=g1",
  "chr1\tfixture\tmRNA\t1\t20\t.\t+\t.\tID=t1;Parent=g1",
  "chr1\tfixture\tmRNA\t1\t20\t.\t+\t.\tID=t2;Parent=g1",
  "chr1\tfixture\texon\t1\t5\t.\t+\t.\tID=e1;Parent=t1,t2",
  "chr1\tfixture\tCDS\t2\t5\t.\t+\t0\tID=c1;Parent=t1"
)
writeLines(gff_lines, gff_file)
shared <- read_gff(gff_file, verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
as.data.frame(shared$data)[c("feature_id", "parent_id", "parent_ids")]
flat <- as_granges(shared, level = "feature")
exons <- as_feature(flat[flat$type == "exon"])
gff_output <- tempfile(fileext = ".gff3")
write_feature(exons, gff_output, keep_attributes = FALSE)
```

Use the grouped view to query all exon and CDS memberships. The shared exon
appears once under each transcript. Its two memberships point to the same
source row. Each group retains the original feature metadata.

```{r annotation-transcript-groups}
grouped <- as_granges(shared, level = "transcript_features")
lengths(grouped)
grouped[["t2"]]
S4Vectors::mcols(grouped)$source_rows
```

For a regional view, restrict the flat ranges while retaining the transcript
declarations needed to resolve GFF3 parent IDs. The grouped positions then
index the restricted Feature table.

```{r annotation-transcript-groups-region}
local_features <- as_feature(IRanges::restrict(flat, start = 2L, end = 4L))
local_groups <- as_granges(local_features, level = "transcript_features")
local_groups
```

`merge_feature(..., conflict = "rename")` updates every parent token using the
same identifier map. Statistics, plots and haplotype location use the established
primary model. Older saved annotations use their single-parent fields in the
grouped view.

BED12 metadata is structural, so edits to spans, block lists or thick intervals
must remain mutually consistent. Invalid edits fail before any output file is
written. Blocks are retained without automatically expanding a new gene model:

```{r annotation-bed12-metadata}
bed_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".bed")
bed_lines <- c(
  "chr1\t0\t20\tt1\t0\t+\t1\t18\t255,0,128\t2\t5,11\t0,9",
  "chr2\t9\t20\tt2\t1000\t-\t9\t9\t0\t1\t11\t0"
)
writeLines(bed_lines, bed_file)
bed_track <- read_bed(bed_file, verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
bed_output <- tempfile(fileext = ".bed12")
write_feature(bed_track, bed_output, format = "bed12")
bed_roundtrip <- read_bed(bed_output, verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
bed_columns <- c(
  "name", "block_count", "block_sizes", "block_starts",
  "thick_start", "thick_end", "item_rgb"
)
as.data.frame(bed_roundtrip$data)[bed_columns]
```

Use standard BED coordinates for interoperable files. The optional `granges`
mode uses explicit closed thick intervals for flat BED12 records, including
end equal to start minus one for empty spans. The legacy gene-model writer's
nonstandard granges convention is unchanged; it cannot disambiguate every
degenerate noncoding span. Header/comments, arbitrary escaped attributes and a
full multi-parent analysis graph remain outside this metadata round trip.
